A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSD research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed layout and expanded appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original RSD benchmark results, efficiency measurements, training ablations, and image reconstructions in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original RSD experiments and ablations and adds qualitative reconstructions and failure examples in Appendices F and H.

M1.justification: The architecture and principal losses are retained. However, Algorithm 1 replaces generator timestep sampling from a fixed subset with sampling from all timesteps 1 through T. This changes the stated procedure, although the retained subset description in Section 3.3 leaves the implemented behavior unclear.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet training and evaluate RealSR, RealSet65, DRealSR, ImageNet-Test, and DIV2K under the retained super-resolution tasks. The added qualitative examples come from benchmarks already evaluated in v1 and do not establish new coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in corresponding quantitative comparisons remain unchanged, including the extended baselines in Appendix D. SiD, FGM, IBMD, and the newly cited DiffInstruct receive discussion rather than new empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 change the sampled diffusion timestep range from 0 through T to 1 through T; Algorithm 1 also changes generator timestep sampling. These are reported training-protocol revisions, without evidence that experiments were rerun. The stated scale factor, crop resolutions, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F extends the single RealSet65 failure example with background-context and fine-detail failures, including ground-truth comparisons on RealSR and DIV2K. This is a limited qualitative extension; the existing multistep-training and supervised-loss ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results continue to be presented as point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 12 revise SUPIR's DIV2K-Val results, including PSNR from 22.18 to 22.13 and MUSIQ from 63.04 to 63.82. Retained RSD benchmark scores are unchanged. Some ablation-specific SSIM results disappear with the SSIM columns in Tables 5–6, while Appendices F and H add qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands the formal treatment: A.1 revises marginalization limits and the trajectory-KL derivation, while new A.2–A.3 add algebraic arguments connecting RSD with SiD, FGM, and IBMD. Proposition 3.1 is retained. The new reformulations nevertheless contain minimization signs inconsistent with Equation (7).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: single-step ResShift distillation, improved perceptual quality over the teacher and SinSR, and competitive quality with better fidelity and lower resource requirements than T2I-based methods.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an explanation attributing superiority over VSD to joint alignment and temporal dependencies. Appendix F expands context and fine-detail limitations, acknowledges cases where T2I methods produce richer backgrounds, and adds societal-impact discussion. Section 4.2 also adds SUPIR's proprietary training data to its proposed explanation of performance differences.

D1.justification: Appendix B revises implementation instructions by removing Algorithm 1's fixed-timestep-subset input and changing sampling ranges. The optimizer settings, loss weights, training hardware and duration, checkpoints, and code/data access links in Appendices C–D remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Previously brief citations to SiD, FGM, and IBMD become detailed comparisons in new Appendices A.2–A.3. v2 explicitly positions RSD as a discrete IBMD-related objective and discusses differences in losses, degradation models, latent-space operation, and architecture size. DiffInstruct is also newly cited.

P1.justification: The main section order and narrative are largely retained, with grammar edits and terminology refinements such as Real-ISR. Appendix A is reorganized into three subsections, and the supplementary overview and limitations heading are updated to reflect the additions.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and v1 Figures 1–2 are merged into v2 Figure 1. Table captions move above the tables, and Tables 5–6 become adjacent displays without SSIM columns. The failure display expands, and four new qualitative figures are added.

improvement.justification: The expanded prior-work comparisons and additional failure examples make v2 more informative. However, new Appendices A.2–A.3 incorrectly turn a negative minimum into a minimum of the negated expression, conflicting with Equation (7). Algorithm 1 also introduces a sampling rule inconsistent with the retained Section 3.3 description. These mathematical and reproducibility inconsistencies offset the explanatory benefits enough that a reliable net quality improvement cannot be established.
